title: GT17-670GD - EVOLVED OPERATIONAL USER INTERFACES (EXPRO+)
description: Existing operational user interfaces for ground segment are primarily built on aging software platforms characterized by deprecated technologies, a monolithic architecture and rigid implementation. While these legacy platforms provide stability for established scenarios, it struggles to adapt to modern operational demands specifically the introduction of remote operations, cloud infrastructure management, and the seamless integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Building on the EGS-CC WebUI and the PulseUI, a specialized WebUI branch tailored for operational environments, the new approach has enabled support for comprehensive UI testing, facilitate remote control capabilities, and better align with the microservices architecture backends. To overcome these challenges and achieve the goals of the project, an architectural and design approach based on the following will be required: - Web-Based Architecture: To guarantee high flexibility and stability. - Unified Design System: Establishing a common look and feel across the ground segment.  - Industry-Standard Framework Principles: Adopting the principles of established UI frameworks (such as Material Design). This will provide a comprehensive suite of reusable components, complete with intuitive documentation and tutorials, hence mitigates the risk of "technology islands".

title: QUANTUM RESISTANT SYMMETRIC-BASED CRYPTOGRAPHIC DEVICE FOR TC/TM PROTECTION - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To implement, validate and test a cryptographic device for security protection of TC/TM.Description:Security protection of TC/TM utilizing cryptographic device capability shall be compliant with correspondingCCSDS standards, implementing SDLS (SpaceData Link Security protocol) and SDLS EP (ExtendedProcedures). It will also include the development of the corresponding Ground Segment Key Management module (unless the needed ground segment capability is already available through COTS or other developments). The implementation will be on hardware; software implementations (not part of this activity) can complement the development for smallsatellites with low assurance requirements or cubesats. The device will target the protection of TC and TM communication links.Theactivity will develop an engineering model, using a hardware based optimised implementations ofauthenticated encryption. Specifically, it will develop:- Engineering Model (EM): flight representative hardware in form, fit and function (including timing and interfaces), allowing functional qualification.- Unit tester / testbench (hardware) that allows to send data to the EM through any of its interfaces up to themaximum data rates supported by the EM (this includes encryption/decryption of data sent/received to the EM).Unit tester / testbench will also record data sent and received to the module.- Ground key management module (software) being ableto manage the cryptographic parameters and keys of the unit tester and EM.

title: SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT ASSESSMENT OF THE ARTES 4.0 PROGRAMME (ARTES FP 1A.138) - EXPRO+

title: SUPPORT TO THE STANDARDISATION OF THE SATELLITE 6G COMPONENT (ARTES FP 1D.029) EXPRO+
description: The purpose of the activity is to coordinate satcom sector involvement in the 6G standardisation process of the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP). The activity scope includes building consensus amongst satcom players, developing contributions to support standardisation actions, and advocating positions favourable to the sector within the standardisation process. The overarching goal being to ensure that the standardisation process results in tangible new opportunities for the satcom industry. In particular, the activity will include support to the Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN)-related work items defined for Release 21 of the 3GPP specification, as well as the preparation of NTN-related items for Release 22 and beyond.

title: HIGH TEMPERATURE HEAT TRANSPORT SYSTEM FOR LUNAR EXPLORATION (HITLUX) - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a high temperature heat transport system for lunar exploration missions, providing an efficientthermal link operating at temperatures in the range of [700degC-1000degC], able to operate within lunarday/night cycles.Description:Sustainable human lunar and planetary exploration relies on effective management of high-temperatureprocesses associated with systems such asIn Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), regenerative fuel cells, andnuclear and chemical heat generation and storage. The temperatures involved are significantly higher than theclassical ranges considered for the design of thermal control subsystems, reaching values of up to 1000degC.In this context, a high-temperature heat transport system is required to ensure effective temperature control through an efficient thermal link operating in the range of [700degC-1000degC]. The developed technology will be compatible with thelunar environment, including potential operational, stand-by and shutdown cycles associated with the lunar day/night periods. As a target, the technology should also be applicable to similar high-temperature systems operating on Mars.This activity aims to develop a breadboard (BB) of a HIgh Temperature heat transport system for LUnareXploration (HITLUX), serving as a technical demonstrator of the feasibility of this technology. The activity is intended to validate the key driving requirements of the system, including anoperating temperature range from 700degC to 1000degC, a heat transport capability up to 700 W over distances of up to 2 m, and withshutdown and start-up capability.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of the HITLUX requirements and elaborationof a technical specification- Review of the state of the art- Trade-offs of various housing materials and working fluids and concept definition- Thermal analysis of the proposed solution- Design of the breadboard(s) and the associated test bench(s)- Manufacture of breadboard(s) and test bench(s)- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Thermal model correlation- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further technology maturation and de-risking.
